source_documents.title: Chalcogen-Substituted Molecular Rotors as Polarity and Viscosity Sensors for Amyloid-β Fibril Formation and Bioimaging

reference_evidence_units.quote: All four compounds displayed pronounced solvatochromism, a hallmark of ICT fluorophores.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 5-8
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Detailed solvent series shown for 6; others in SI.

reference_evidence_units.quote: reveals that the emission of these chromone rotors originates from an ICT transition between the HOMO and LUMO
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 5-8
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emissive transition has ICT character; gap narrows from 5 to 8.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In polar, low-viscosity media such as PBS, stabilization of the charge-separated configuration facilitates rotation about the D–π–A bond, promoting formation of a TICT state with reduced D–A orbital overlap and suppressed radiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 5-8
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weak emission in PBS attributed to rotation into a dark TICT state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: All compounds exhibit a linear increase in absorption and emission intensity with increasing the concentration (5–50 µM) without the appearance of new bands or spectral distortions
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 5-8
reference_evidence_units.statement: No dye aggregation in PBS at working concentrations.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Only this concentration range in PBS.

reference_evidence_units.quote: in high-viscosity media, this rotation is suppressed, favoring the brighter ICT emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 5-8
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity turn-on attributed to suppressed rotation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: compound 5 displayed a smaller overall enhancement (∼50-fold from water to 100% glycerol)
reference_evidence_units.subject: 5 (O)
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Glycerol also lowers polarity relative to water.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Viscosity turn-on of a molecular rotor: restricted twisting suppresses the dark TICT channel.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: ICT emission with polarity-stabilised TICT quenching.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No intramolecular proton donor-acceptor pair (no OH/NH next to an acceptor).

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No aggregation in PBS at 5-50 µM (linear absorption/emission, no new bands).

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No heavy atom; the heavy-atom ISC argument is made only for the S/Se/Te analogues.

environment_context.effect: binding to amyloid fibrils and viscous cellular regions immobilises the rotor

contrast_group.factor: chalcogen in the chromone acceptor (O / Se / Te)
contrast_group.paper_difference: emission falls O > S > Se > Te; Se/Te quenching attributed to heavy-atom ISC; viscosity response largest for S/Se
